why: The quoted sentence EXISTS VERBATIM (hosting.md line 341, 'Known limitations' table, row 'No per-subagent wall-clock deadline'; whole line read, the second half does not reverse it). The cited file:line is also real: subagent-tool.ts:605-616 is the background-dispatch return and the Pi orchestrator has no output-idle timer there. The finding still fails on four counts. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the exact trap named in inert-worklist section 4 item 4. agent-sdk/hosting.md governs the Claude Agent SDK, and CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS is a knob of the Claude Code binary itself. This fork vendors that binary and the implementation is live inside it: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude contains 'g=je.CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS||600000' inside the async-agent loop (adjacent to turnStartTime, setMode("responding"), shouldNotifyOwner). Nessy does not scrub it: claude-agent.ts:915 deletes only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. So on the backend this page is about, the stall watchdog is present and honoured with its 600000 ms default. The consequence ('no stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents') is therefore false for the subsystem the doc names, and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts is Nessy's own Pi orchestration, not an Agent SDK run_in_background subagent. (2) THE CLAIMED POSITIVE CONTROL IS FALSE. The finding asserts grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog' over packages/shared/src, packages/pi-agent-server/src and packages/server-core/src 'returns no match'. It does match, in a named directory: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6076 ('truly hung subprocesses are caught by the stdio death watchdog') and, substantively, packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:230-419, which implements a real two-timer connect watchdog with an explicit IDLE arm (createConnectWatchdog(connectIdleMs, connectCeilingMs), watchdog.kick(), Promise.race([client.connect(transport), watchdog.promise])). An absence claim whose own grep is demonstrably wrong does not stand. (3) THE DOC'S PRIMARY PRESCRIPTION IS IMPLEMENTED. The row is a documented LIMITATION of the SDK, not a required feature, and its first sentence is 'Cap each subagent with maxTurns in its AgentDefinition.' Nessy carries maxTurns end to end: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:401/418-419/451 validates it (positive integer, string-or-number), packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:163 carries it onto the descriptor, and spawner.ts:571-574 forwards it with the comment 'The host enforces maxTurns and clamps permissionMode against the parent'. So the named mitigation is built on the Pi path too, and the claim that the run is 'bounded only by the abort signal' is wrong on top of maxTurns, stop_task and the capability-generation teardown reachable through registerBackgroundChildTask's BackgroundTaskRegistry entry. (4) THE CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR EMBELLISHES THE DOC. The page says only that the watchdog 'fires'; 'aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result' appears nowhere on the page. Finally, this is not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3, and it is not a deliberate product difference (subscription-flow drop, gateway targeting, NESSY_ rename) - it is refuted on subsystem misattribution plus a false absence, not on scope. The coverage map already verdicts agent-sdk/hosting as green, 'all built' via R6.
correctedState: The Claude Agent SDK's own stall watchdog is present in this fork, because the fork vendors the Claude Code binary that implements it: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude reads CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS with a 600000 ms default in its async-agent loop, and Nessy passes the environment through untouched (claude-agent.ts:915 deletes only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). The doc row's primary prescription, maxTurns in AgentDefinition, is implemented on the Pi path as well: validated at packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:401/418-419/451, carried at packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:163, forwarded and host-enforced per spawner.ts:571-574. What is genuinely absent is narrower and belongs to a different subsystem: Nessy's own Pi orchestrator (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:585-617 plus background-child-task.ts) has no output-idle timer of its own and no NESSY_-prefixed analogue of the env var, so a Pi background subagent that goes silent without exhausting maxTurns is bounded only by maxTurns, stop_task and the abort signal. Note also that the repo does have idle watchdogs elsewhere (packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:230-419 is a two-timer connect watchdog with an idle arm), so any absence claim here must be scoped to the Pi orchestrator rather than stated repo-wide.
